title: What is the length of the black line?
description: A number line from zero to two has each unit cut into two equal halves, and a black line runs past one. The board counts the halves under the black line, multiplies the count by one half and checks that the line is one whole and one more half.
teaching_notes: One idea: a line longer than one unit is still its count of equal parts times one part. Watch for students who count only the parts after one.

video_script.why: A learner finds the length of a line that is longer than one unit by counting equal halves from zero.
video_script.substitution: the book's own number line from 0 to 2 with each unit cut into two equal parts
video_script.anchor: the number line from 0 to 2 with each unit cut into two equal parts, a blue line to one half and a black line past one
video_script.payoff_line: The black line is three halves of a unit long
maths_rules: 1 unit cut into 2 equal parts: each part is 1/2 unit
the black line covers 3 parts from 0: 2 parts up to 1 and 1 more part
check: 2 halves make 1 whole, and one more half is added
video_script.design: One number line from zero to two with a half-unit blue line already drawn. The black line is counted part by part past the mark one.

<bookmark mark='more'/>One more part lies after one. The line covers three parts in all.

narration: <bookmark mark='times'/>Step three, the length is the count times the size of one part. That is three times one half.

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, two halves make one whole unit. The black line goes one more half past one, so it is longer than one unit.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The black line is three halves of a unit long.
It is one whole unit and one more half.
